title: Amos Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Amos chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Amos Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Amos Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Amos 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The Lord GOD showed Amos grasshoppers
The Lord GOD called to contend by fire
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord GOD showed Amos grasshoppers
questions.explanation: This event occurs first as stated in Amos 7:1, where it mentions the Lord showing Amos the grasshoppers.

questions.question: What did Amos see that the Lord formed in Amos 7:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Grasshoppers
questions.explanation: Amos 7:1 states that the Lord formed grasshoppers.

questions.question: What did Amos ask the Lord after the grasshoppers had eaten the grass of the land?
questions.correctAnswer: By whom shall Jacob arise?
questions.explanation: In Amos 7:2, Amos beseeches the Lord by asking, 'by whom shall Jacob arise?'.

questions.question: What did the Lord do in response to Amos's plea in Amos 7:3?
questions.correctAnswer: He repented for this
questions.explanation: Amos 7:3 states that the Lord repented for this.

questions.question: What did the Lord call to contend by in Amos 7:4?
questions.correctAnswer: Fire
questions.explanation: Amos 7:4 mentions that the Lord called to contend by fire.

questions.question: What did the fire eat up according to Amos 7:4?
questions.correctAnswer: The great deep
questions.explanation: Amos 7:4 specifies that the fire devoured the great deep.

questions.question: What did Amos plead with the Lord to do in Amos 7:5?
questions.correctAnswer: Cease, I beseech thee
questions.explanation: In Amos 7:5, Amos asks the Lord to cease, saying, 'cease, I beseech thee'.

questions.question: What was the Lord's reaction in Amos 7:6?
questions.correctAnswer: He repented for this
questions.explanation: Amos 7:6 indicates that the Lord repented for this.

questions.question: What does the Lord say will not happen in Amos 7:3?
questions.correctAnswer: It shall not be
questions.explanation: Amos 7:3 states, 'It shall not be, saith the LORD'.

questions.question: What does Amos refer to Jacob as in Amos 7:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Small
questions.explanation: In Amos 7:2, Amos refers to Jacob as 'for he is small'.

questions.question: In Amos 7:4, what did the fire eat up?
questions.correctAnswer: A part
questions.explanation: Amos 7:4 notes that the fire 'did eat up a part'.

questions.question: The Lord repented for the fire in Amos 7:6.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: According to Amos 7:6, the Lord repented for this.

questions.question: Amos asked the Lord to forgive him in Amos 7:2.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Amos 7:2 states that he said, 'O Lord GOD, forgive, I beseech thee'.

questions.question: Amos saw a vision of a lion in Amos 7:1.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Amos 7:1 mentions grasshoppers, not a lion.

questions.question: The Lord called to contend by wind in Amos 7:4.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Amos 7:4 states that the Lord called to contend by fire, not wind.

medium.title: Amos Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Amos Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did the Lord stand upon when He showed Amos in Amos 7:7?
options: A wall made by a plumbline
questions.correctAnswer: A wall made by a plumbline
questions.explanation: Amos 7:7 states, 'the Lord stood upon a wall made by a plumbline, with a plumbline in his hand.'

questions.question: What does Amos 7:8 promise will happen if someone sees the plumbline as commanded in Amos 7:7?
options: God will set a plumbline in the midst of Israel and not pass by them any more
Jeroboam will build more high places
questions.correctAnswer: God will set a plumbline in the midst of Israel and not pass by them any more
questions.explanation: Amos 7:8 says the Lord will set a plumbline in the midst of Israel and will not pass by them any more, following the vision of the plumbline in Amos 7:7.

questions.question: According to Amos 7:9, what will happen to the high places of Isaac?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be desolate
questions.explanation: Amos 7:9 states, 'And the high places of Isaac shall be desolate,' indicating their destruction.

questions.question: What connection is found between Amos 7:10 and Amos 7:11 regarding Amaziah's message to Jeroboam?
options: Amos is accused of conspiracy and his prophecy of Jeroboam’s death is cited
Amaziah praises Amos and supports his prophecy
Jeroboam is told to ignore Amos completely
Amaziah asks Amos to prophesy in Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Amos is accused of conspiracy and his prophecy of Jeroboam’s death is cited
questions.explanation: Amos 7:10 shows Amaziah accusing Amos of conspiracy, and Amos 7:11 cites Amos's prophecy that Jeroboam shall die by the sword.

questions.question: What practical lesson can Christians learn from the Lord showing Amos the plumbline in Amos 7:7?
options: God measures the integrity of His people and holds them accountable
God rewards those who build walls
God ignores the sins of the people
questions.correctAnswer: God measures the integrity of His people and holds them accountable
questions.explanation: The plumbline symbolizes God’s standard of righteousness, showing He evaluates His people’s faithfulness (Amos 7:7).

questions.question: How does Amos 7:8 emphasize God's justice toward Israel?
options: By stating He will not pass by them any more
questions.correctAnswer: By stating He will not pass by them any more
questions.explanation: Amos 7:8 indicates God will no longer overlook Israel’s sins, reinforcing His just judgment.

questions.question: What consequence does Amos 7:9 warn regarding the sanctuaries of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be laid waste
questions.explanation: Amos 7:9 explicitly states the sanctuaries of Israel will be destroyed as part of God’s judgment.

questions.question: What practical advice does Amaziah the priest give to Amos in Amos 7:12?
options: Go to Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy
Stay in Bethel and stop prophesying
questions.correctAnswer: Go to Judah, eat bread there, and prophesy
questions.explanation: Amos 7:12 records Amaziah telling Amos to leave Israel and prophesy in Judah instead.

questions.question: What does the accusation in Amos 7:10 reveal about the reaction of religious leaders to prophetic messages?
options: They may reject and accuse prophets of conspiracy
questions.correctAnswer: They may reject and accuse prophets of conspiracy
questions.explanation: Amaziah accuses Amos of conspiracy, showing how leaders sometimes oppose difficult prophetic truths (Amos 7:10).

questions.question: From Amos 7:11, what is the predicted fate of Israel?
options: Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land
Israel will be victorious over enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Israel shall surely be led away captive out of their own land
questions.explanation: Amos 7:11 prophesies Israel’s exile as a consequence of their sins.

questions.question: How does Amos 7:8-9 connect God's judgment with the spiritual state of Israel?
options: God sets a plumbline to measure Israel and announces desolation of their high places
God promises Israel prosperity and peace
questions.correctAnswer: God sets a plumbline to measure Israel and announces desolation of their high places
questions.explanation: Amos 7:8-9 shows God’s judgment both symbolized by the plumbline and expressed in the destruction of Israel’s sacred places.

questions.question: What practical challenge does Amos 7:12 pose for believers when facing opposition?
options: Believers may be told to leave familiar places but must continue their calling elsewhere
Believers should stop speaking the truth
Believers should seek to please all people
questions.correctAnswer: Believers may be told to leave familiar places but must continue their calling elsewhere
questions.explanation: Amaziah’s instruction in Amos 7:12 challenges Amos to relocate but not to cease prophesying, highlighting perseverance.

questions.question: Why did Amos plead for forgiveness in Amos 7:2 and Amos 7:5?
options: Because he recognized Jacob (Israel) was small and vulnerable
Because he wanted to stop prophesying
questions.correctAnswer: Because he recognized Jacob (Israel) was small and vulnerable
questions.explanation: In Amos 7:2 and 7:5, Amos asks God to forgive because Jacob is weak and in need of help.

questions.question: True or False: According to Amos 7:3 and Amos 7:6, the Lord repented and did not bring the punishments He had shown Amos.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Both Amos 7:3 and 7:6 state that the Lord repented and the judgments were not carried out at those times.

questions.question: True or False: Amaziah welcomed Amos warmly and encouraged his prophetic ministry in Bethel according to Amos 7:10-12.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Amos 7:10-12 shows Amaziah opposing Amos, accusing him of conspiracy and telling him to leave Bethel.

hard.title: Amos Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Amos Chapter 7.

questions.question: What reason does Amaziah give for telling Amos not to prophesy again at Bethel?
options: For it is the king's chapel, and it is the king's court
Because the people will not listen
Because Amos is not a true prophet
Because Bethel is a sacred place for Israel
questions.correctAnswer: For it is the king's chapel, and it is the king's court
questions.explanation: Amos 7:13 states, 'But prophesy not again any more at Bethel: for it is the king's chapel, and it is the king's court.' This is the reason Amaziah gives.

questions.question: How does Amos describe his background in response to Amaziah's accusation?
options: I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit
I was trained by the priests in Bethel
I was a prophet from my youth
I was a scribe and teacher of the law
questions.correctAnswer: I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit
questions.explanation: Amos 7:14 shows Amos's humble origins: 'I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit.'

questions.question: What calling did the LORD give to Amos according to Amos 7:15?
options: Go, prophesy unto my people Israel
Be a priest in the temple
Write the law for the kings
questions.correctAnswer: Go, prophesy unto my people Israel
questions.explanation: Amos 7:15 states, 'And the LORD said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel,' indicating his divine commission.

questions.question: What is the content of the word of the LORD that Amos declares to Amaziah in Amos 7:16?
options: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac
Thou shalt be king over Israel
The land will prosper under your watch
The temple will be rebuilt soon
questions.correctAnswer: Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac
questions.explanation: Amos 7:16 records God's word through Amos: 'Thou sayest, Prophesy not against Israel, and drop not thy word against the house of Isaac.'

questions.question: According to Amos 7:17, what are the predicted consequences for Amaziah and Israel?
options: Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, thy sons and daughters shall fall by the sword, thy land shall be divided, and thou shalt die in a polluted land
Thou shalt reign in peace and prosper
The temple shall be cleansed and restored
Thy family shall be blessed and multiply
questions.correctAnswer: Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, thy sons and daughters shall fall by the sword, thy land shall be divided, and thou shalt die in a polluted land
questions.explanation: Amos 7:17 prophesies severe judgment: 'Thy wife shall be an harlot in the city, and thy sons and thy daughters shall fall by the sword, and thy land shall be divided by line; and thou shalt die in a polluted land.'

questions.question: What occupation did Amos have before being called to prophesy?
options: Herdsman and gatherer of sycomore fruit
Fisherman on the Sea of Galilee
questions.correctAnswer: Herdsman and gatherer of sycomore fruit
questions.explanation: As stated in Amos 7:14, Amos was 'an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit' before his prophetic call.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'ro’eh' (רֹאֶה) in Amos 7:14 mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Seer or prophet
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'ro’eh' means 'seer' or 'prophet,' indicating one who receives divine visions, relevant to Amos's role (Amos 7:14).

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Amos 7:7-8 with the imagery of a plumbline?
questions.correctAnswer: Symbolism
questions.explanation: Amos 7:7-8 uses the plumbline as a symbol for God's standard of righteousness and judgment against Israel.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's judgment on Israel as seen in Amos 7:17?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 23:37-39
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:37-39 echoes the theme of judgment and captivity for Israel similar to Amos 7:17's prophecy of exile.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to the theme of Amos being a non-professional prophet called by God, as in Amos 7:14-15?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 1:4-10
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 1:4-10 describes God's calling of Jeremiah, a non-professional prophet, paralleling Amos 7:14-15's calling of Amos.

questions.question: What event precedes Amos being told not to prophesy at Bethel by Amaziah?
options: Amaziah sending a message to King Jeroboam accusing Amos of conspiracy
The LORD standing by a wall with a plumbline
questions.correctAnswer: Amaziah sending a message to King Jeroboam accusing Amos of conspiracy
questions.explanation: Amos 7:10-12 describe Amaziah sending a message to Jeroboam accusing Amos before Amos is told not to prophesy at Bethel (7:13).

questions.question: Which literary device is used in Amos 7:17 to convey the severity of the judgment against Amaziah and his family?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Amos 7:17 uses parallelism in listing the judgments on Amaziah's wife, children, land, and death to emphasize the comprehensive nature of the punishment.

questions.question: How does the prophetic interaction between Amos and Amaziah illustrate a typology found in prophetic confrontations throughout the Old Testament?
options: Conflict between true prophetic word and official religious authority
Peaceful cooperation between prophet and priest
questions.correctAnswer: Conflict between true prophetic word and official religious authority
questions.explanation: Amos 7:10-17 shows the tension between Amos's divine message and Amaziah's priestly opposition, a common typology in OT prophetic narratives.

questions.question: True or False: According to Amos 7:15, Amos was divinely chosen by God while he was following the flock as a herdsman.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Amos 7:15 states, 'And the LORD took me as I followed the flock,' confirming divine calling during his herdsman occupation.

questions.question: True or False: Amos was encouraged by Amaziah to continue prophesying at Bethel as it was a holy and acceptable place for prophecy.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Amos 7:13 shows Amaziah forbidding Amos from prophesying at Bethel, calling it the king's chapel and court, not a place for Amos's prophecy.

theological.title: Amos Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Amos Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Amos 7:3 teach about God's nature?
options: God repents and changes His mind in response to intercession
God is immutable and never changes His decrees
God is indifferent to human pleas
God always executes judgment without mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God repents and changes His mind in response to intercession
questions.explanation: Amos 7:3 states, 'The LORD repented for this: It shall not be, saith the LORD,' showing that God can relent in judgment when petitioned.

questions.question: What doctrine regarding divine judgment is taught in Amos 7:9?
options: God holds His people accountable and will bring desolation for their idolatry
God will always protect the sanctuaries regardless of Israel’s sin
Judgment will only come upon foreign nations, not Israel
Israel’s high places are inviolable as God’s holy sites
questions.correctAnswer: God holds His people accountable and will bring desolation for their idolatry
questions.explanation: Amos 7:9 declares that 'the high places of Isaac shall be desolate' and 'sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste,' indicating accountability for Israel’s idolatry.

questions.question: What doctrine about prophetic calling is revealed in Amos 7:14?
options: Prophetic ministry can arise from ordinary backgrounds by divine call
Only sons of prophets can be prophets
Prophets must be formally trained priests
Herdsmen and farmers cannot be called to prophesy
questions.correctAnswer: Prophetic ministry can arise from ordinary backgrounds by divine call
questions.explanation: Amos 7:14 shows Amos stating he was not a prophet or prophet’s son, but a herdsman, yet God called him to prophesy to Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Amos 7:7 specifically demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: In Amos 7:7, God standing with a plumbline symbolizes His sovereign authority to measure and judge Israel’s moral and covenantal standing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is emphasized in Amos 7:6?
questions.correctAnswer: Longsuffering
questions.explanation: Amos 7:6 states 'The LORD repented for this,' indicating God's patience and willingness to relent from judgment upon intercession.

questions.question: How does Amos 7:8 connect to the broader redemptive theme of covenant judgment in Scripture?
options: It demonstrates God's enforcement of covenant standards through judgment
It portrays covenant blessings without consequences
It denies God's involvement in human history
It shows God abandoning His covenant people
questions.correctAnswer: It demonstrates God's enforcement of covenant standards through judgment
questions.explanation: Amos 7:8’s plumbline metaphor signifies God's setting a standard for Israel, resonating with covenantal themes of blessing and judgment found throughout Scripture.

questions.question: In what way does Amos 7:17 anticipate New Testament themes of judgment and exile?
options: It foreshadows the judgment and dispersion of God's people due to covenant unfaithfulness
It promises immediate restoration without judgment
It denies any future exile for Israel
It focuses solely on personal sin without national consequences
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows the judgment and dispersion of God's people due to covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Amos 7:17’s prophecy of captivity and division anticipates themes in the New Testament where judgment follows persistent covenant violation.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Amos 7:1 and Amos 7:4 teach about God's judgment?
options: God’s judgment is both consuming and purifying, aimed at correction
God’s judgment is arbitrary and without purpose
God only uses natural disasters to judge
God’s judgment is always final and without possibility of reprieve
questions.correctAnswer: God’s judgment is both consuming and purifying, aimed at correction
questions.explanation: Verses Amos 7:1 and 7:4 describe judgment by grasshoppers and fire consuming parts of the land, indicating God’s judgment is active, purifying, and purposeful.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Amos 7:10 and Amos 7:13 reveal about human opposition to prophetic truth?
options: Prophets will face political and institutional resistance when confronting sin
Prophets are always welcomed and supported by leaders
Prophecy is only accepted in private and never public settings
Prophets must avoid addressing political matters
questions.correctAnswer: Prophets will face political and institutional resistance when confronting sin
questions.explanation: Amos 7:10 and 7:13 show Amaziah accusing Amos and forbidding prophecy at Bethel, illustrating opposition from religious and royal authorities.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine calling and human response is found in Amos 7:14 and Amos 7:15?
options: God calls individuals from ordinary backgrounds, and obedience to that call is essential
Only professional clergy receive divine calling
One can refuse God’s call without consequence
Divine callings are always public and dramatic
questions.correctAnswer: God calls individuals from ordinary backgrounds, and obedience to that call is essential
questions.explanation: Amos 7:14–15 shows Amos’ humble origins and God’s direct commissioning, highlighting the necessity of faithful response to divine calling.

questions.question: What does Amos 7:1–6 actually teach in response to sceptics claiming God’s repentance shows inconsistency in His nature?
options: God’s repentance reveals His relational responsiveness and covenantal mercy
God is inconsistent and unreliable in His decrees
God’s repentance means He makes mistakes
God vacillates without purpose in His decisions
questions.correctAnswer: God’s repentance reveals His relational responsiveness and covenantal mercy
questions.explanation: Amos 7:1–6 shows God relenting after intercession, not due to mistake but as an expression of merciful interaction within covenant relationship.

questions.question: What doctrine does Amos 7:2 teach about human sin and its impact on Israel's future?
options: The smallness of Jacob reflects Israel’s vulnerability due to sin
Jacob’s status is irrelevant to God's plans
Sin has no effect on Israel's future
Israel’s future is guaranteed regardless of behavior
questions.correctAnswer: The smallness of Jacob reflects Israel’s vulnerability due to sin
questions.explanation: Amos 7:2 expresses concern for Jacob’s frailty, theologically pointing to the consequences of sin diminishing Israel's strength and hope.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Amos 7:16 concerning God’s judgment on His prophet’s opponents?
questions.correctAnswer: Justice
questions.explanation: Amos 7:16 pronounces God’s judgment on Amaziah, emphasizing His attribute of executing righteous justice on those opposing His word.

questions.question: How does Amos 7:11 contribute to the narrative arc of Israel’s exile and restoration in Scripture?
options: It prophesies the coming judgment and exile as consequences of covenant unfaithfulness
It denies any future exile for Israel
It promises immediate restoration without judgment
It focuses only on personal repentance without national implications
questions.correctAnswer: It prophesies the coming judgment and exile as consequences of covenant unfaithfulness
questions.explanation: Amos 7:11 predicts Jeroboam’s death and Israel’s captivity, connecting to broader biblical themes of exile due to covenant breach.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about divine judgment and human agency is taught in Amos 7:12 and Amos 7:13?
options: Human authorities may reject God’s word, but divine sovereignty ensures prophecy will be fulfilled
Prophets should always obey human leaders over God
God’s word depends on human approval to be effective
Prophecy is merely political speech without divine authority
questions.correctAnswer: Human authorities may reject God’s word, but divine sovereignty ensures prophecy will be fulfilled
questions.explanation: Amos 7:12–13 shows Amaziah’s attempt to silence Amos, but God’s sovereign call overrides human opposition.
